content:
Oscar two-time and Golden Globe four-time winner Sally Field (莎莉·菲爾德), at an Emmy Awards ceremony largely devoid of politics, appeared to take a veiled jab at President Donald Trump's provocations toward Canada.

This two-time Oscar and four-time Golden Globe winner (translator's note: the original text says Emmy Awards, which should be a typo) had just won for her role in "Remarkably Bright Creatures," and immediately shifted the topic northward.

She specifically paid tribute to cinematographer Ashley Connor, saying she "turned the Pacific Northwest into another character — and that's Canada now!"

She said meaningfully: "Blessed Canada — our neighbor, our friend," and the room erupted in applause, with anti-Trump activist Mark Ruffalo (麥克·雷法路) among the audience.

President Trump has spent much of his second term distancing himself from this neighboring ally. He reignited the trade war and escalated tensions by renaming Lake Ontario as "Lake America" in an executive order. He has also repeatedly threatened to annex Canada as the 51st state of the United States.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney (馬克·卡尼) said: "We have all seen America changing — its trade relationships, its foreign policy, its national monuments, and even its place names. Canadians are clear: the name that reflects reality is Lake Ontario — it was, it is, and it always will be."

Field won Best Actress in a Limited Series or Anthology Movie, and also appeared to comment on the Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. merger. The US$110 billion deal has stalled amid lawsuits filed by 12 states, including entertainment heavyweights California and New York, over concerns the merger would harm competition.

Field said: "For 62 years, I have been so grateful and so proud to be part of the artistic community. With art, we matter. Our voices matter. Our diversity, our unique storytelling — these all matter. We cannot let these voices be silenced, compromised, or merged."
